findings.title: Stage-1 SFT trainer regresses raw velocity to HQ latent, not x0
findings.quote:
def predict_sample(*args, **kwargs):
    output = forward(*args, **kwargs)
    sample = output[0]
    hidden_states = kwargs["hidden_states"]
    timesteps = kwargs["timestep"]
    alpha = scheduler.alphas_cumprod.to(
        device=hidden_states.device, dtype=hidden_states.dtype
    )[timesteps].sqrt()
    while alpha.ndim < hidden_states.ndim:
        alpha = alpha.unsqueeze(-1)
    sigma = (1.0 - alpha.square()).sqrt()
    prediction = (alpha * hidden_states - sample) / sigma
    return (prediction,) + output[1:]
findings.claim: The SFT trainer wraps transformer.forward so it returns prediction=(alpha*z_t - v)/sigma. The inherited compute_loss then applies get_velocity(prediction, z_t) = alpha*z_t - sigma*prediction, which algebraically collapses to the RAW velocity v; the MSE loss therefore compares v to the HQ latent, not x0 = alpha*z_t - sigma*v (Eq. 2).
findings.concern: Inference (inference_script.py:491) and the LoRA trainer (lora_one_s1_trainer.py:200-207) both decode x0 = alpha*z_t - sigma*v, but the SFT trainer (the documented main path, --training_type sft) optimizes v -> HQ latent, a different and inconsistent objective — so a model trained with the released SFT code would not match what the pipeline decodes at test time.
findings.resolution: Confirm the intended Stage-1 SFT target: predict_sample should either be the identity (let get_velocity produce x0, matching the LoRA path) or the get_velocity call should be dropped for SFT. Verify with _audit_code/check_sft_target.py which reproduces the collapse to v.
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at lines 13-25; predict_sample returns (alpha*z_t - v)/sigma, and the inherited compute_loss at lora_one_s1_trainer.py:200-207 (confirmed by inspection) calls get_velocity(prediction, z_t) which per its inline comment computes alpha*z_t - sigma*prediction = v, so MSE(v, hq_latent) is the actual loss.

findings.title: paired_random_crop_video draws independent LQ temporal index, misaligning HR/LR pairs
findings.quote:
# Randomly sample temporal index
start_idx = random.randint(0, len(hq_frames) - num_frames)
lq_start_idx = random.randint(0, len(lq_frames) - num_frames)

# Crop frames
cropped_hq = [
    f[top_hq:top_hq + hq_crop_h, left_hq:left_hq + hq_crop_w, :]
    for f in hq_frames[start_idx:start_idx + num_frames]
]
cropped_lq = [
    f[top:top + lq_crop_h, left:left + lq_crop_w, :]
    for f in lq_frames[lq_start_idx:lq_start_idx + num_frames]
]
findings.claim: The temporal crop uses two INDEPENDENT random start indices (start_idx for HQ, lq_start_idx for LQ) even though len(hq_frames)==len(lq_frames) is asserted and LQ is the per-frame degradation of HQ; the spatial crop is correctly scale-aligned but the temporal window is not.
findings.concern: The HR target clip and LR input clip come from different temporal offsets of the same video (~91% of the time, mean 3.6-frame offset for the Stage-1 25/35 config), so the model is trained to map LR frames to non-corresponding HR frames — directly corrupting the one-step LR->HR regression the method depends on; the function's own docstring says frames are 'aligned'.
findings.resolution: Use a single shared start index (cropped_lq should index lq_frames[start_idx:start_idx+num_frames]). Confirm with _audit_code/check_temporal_misalign.py. This routine is used by both Stage-1 (real_sr_dataset.py:261) and Stage-2 (real_sr_image_video_dataset.py:256).
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at lines 480-492; two independent random.randint calls for start_idx and lq_start_idx are plainly present in the code.

findings.title: eval_dover.py assigns dover_results[i-1], shifting per-sample DOVER by one
findings.quote:
for i, name in enumerate(pred_names):
    results[name] = dover_results[i-1]
findings.claim: Per-sample DOVER scores are keyed by name using index i-1 instead of i, so the first video name receives the LAST video's score and every name is shifted by one position.
findings.concern: Per-video DOVER attribution is wrong; the reported dataset AVERAGE (np.mean over all results) is unaffected because the assignment is a cyclic permutation of the same value set, so Table 2/Table 3 averages are not changed, but any per-sample analysis/logging is corrupted.
findings.resolution: Change dover_results[i-1] to dover_results[i]. See _audit_code/check_dover_offbyone.py (10/10 per-sample mismatches, average preserved).
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at lines 158-159; dover_results[i-1] is present exactly as claimed.

findings.title: Stage-2 (pixel-space) trainer and its DISTS/frame losses are absent
findings.claim: The Stage-2 launcher requests model_name 'dove-s2', but only 'dove-s1' is registered (lora_one_s1_trainer.py:384, sft_one_s1_trainer.py:31); train.py:13 get_model_cls('dove-s2','sft') therefore raises 'Model dove-s2 is not supported'. No trainer implements compute_loss(batch, mode): the only concrete compute_loss (lora_one_s1_trainer.py:116) is pure latent MSE. self.dists_loss is created in prepare_for_training (trainer.py:424-426) but never consumed by any loss, and frame_diff_weight (args.py:118, passed =1.0 by the launcher) is referenced nowhere in Python.
findings.concern: Stage-2 'Refinement' — pixel-space mixed image/video training with the perceptual DISTS loss (Eq. 4) and the frame-difference loss L_frame (Eq. 6-7) — is half of the paper's 'latent–pixel training strategy' contribution and underlies Table 1a (rows S1+S2-I, S1+S2-I/V) and the Table 1b image-ratio ablation; none of it can be run or reproduced from the released code, and `bash train_ddp_one_s2.sh` crashes at startup.
findings.resolution: Release the dove-s2 trainer that registers under model_name 'dove-s2', implements compute_loss(batch, mode), and applies MSE + λ1·DISTS + λ2·L_frame. See _audit_code/check_stage2_missing.py (dove-s2 registered nowhere; frame_diff_weight unused; dists_loss never consumed).
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at line 9; repo-wide grep finds 'dove-s2' only in the launcher itself — it is never passed to register() anywhere, so the model_name is unrecognised at runtime.

findings.title: E*warp and FasterVQA computation not runnable / absent
findings.quote:
original_dir = os.getcwd()
raft_dir = os.path.join(original_dir, "RAFT")
os.chdir(raft_dir)
from ewarp import Ewarp as Ewarp
findings.claim: eval_ewarp.py chdir's into '<script_dir>/RAFT' (which does not exist — RAFT lives at finetune/utils/RAFT) and imports module 'ewarp', which is present nowhere in the repo; the script cannot run. There is no script anywhere that computes FasterVQA (only referenced in README).
findings.concern: The E*warp (temporal-consistency, 6 datasets) and FasterVQA (7 datasets) columns of the main comparison Table 2 have no runnable computation in the repo, so those reported numbers cannot be reproduced from the released code.
findings.resolution: Provide the missing ewarp.py (and correct the RAFT path) and a FasterVQA script. Note: the README already lists 'Add metric computation scripts for FasterVQA, DOVER, and Ewarp' as a TODO, so this is partly acknowledged.
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at lines 146-149; ewarp.py is absent from the repo (find found nothing), RAFT exists only at finetune/utils/RAFT (wrong path), and no FasterVQA script exists anywhere in the repo.

findings.title: Only Stage-1 launcher points training data at the UDM10 evaluation set
findings.claim: The only provided Stage-1 launcher sets the training data_root/video_column to the UDM10 test set — the same dataset used to report every Table 1 ablation number and the UDM10 rows of Table 2.
findings.concern: If taken literally this trains Stage-1 on the evaluation set (leakage); however it is more likely a leftover template default (the README's workflow trains on HQ-VSR via prepare_dataset.py, and the Stage-2 launcher correctly uses ../datasets/train/HQ-VSR.txt).
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm the actual Stage-1 training corpus (HQ-VSR per Sec. 4.1) and that UDM10 here is only a placeholder, i.e. that no reported model was trained on a benchmark it is evaluated on.
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at lines 27-28; data_root pointing to test/UDM10 is exactly as claimed, and the concern is appropriately hedged as a question.
